textbookBox.concept: Let us begin with the tortoise. It walks 1/4 km in 1 hour, so in 3 hours the distance is 3 × 1/4 km, which is 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 = 3/4 km.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: Let us begin with the tortoise. It walks 1/4 km in 1 hour, so in 3 hours the distance is 3 × 1/4 km, which is 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 = 3/4 km. Multiplication works the same way even when the distance in one hour is a fraction.
beats.speakEn: Let us begin with the tortoise. It walks 1/4 km in 1 hour, so in 3 hours the distance is 3  times  1/4 km, which is 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4  equals  3/4 km. Multiplication works the same way even when the distance in one hour is a fraction.

beats.en: What happens when both numbers are fractions? The tortoise walks 1/4 km in an hour. How far in half an hour? That is 1/2 × 1/4. We draw a unit square to stand for one whole and shade 1/4 of it.
beats.speakEn: What happens when both numbers are fractions? The tortoise walks 1/4 km in an hour. How far in half an hour? That is 1/2  times  1/4. We draw a unit square to stand for one whole and shade 1/4 of it.

Rule: What happens when both numbers are fractions? The tortoise walks 1/4 km in an hour.

textbookBox.concept: When two unit fractions are multiplied, such as 1/18 × 1/12, the whole is divided into 18 rows and 12 columns, so the product is 1/(18 × 12) = 1/216.

beats.en: When two unit fractions are multiplied, such as 1/18 × 1/12, the whole is divided into 18 rows and 12 columns, so the product is 1/(18 × 12) = 1/216.
beats.speakEn: When two unit fractions are multiplied, such as 1/18  times  1/12, the whole is divided into 18 rows and 12 columns, so the product is 1/(18  times  12)  equals  1/216.

beats.en: Multiplying big numbers and simplifying afterwards is slow. Take 12/7 × 5/24. Instead of computing 60/168, notice that 12 is a factor of both the numerator 12 and the denominator 24.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 7 maths · Working with Fractions · Complete Summary
textbookBox.concept: When we multiply two counting numbers bigger than 1, such as 3 × 5 = 15, the product is greater than both numbers. With fractions this is not always true. Multiply 1/4 × 8 = 2.

beats.en: Let us review the key takeaway from Working with Fractions: When we multiply two counting numbers bigger than 1, such as 3 × 5 = 15, the product is greater than both numbers. With fractions this is not always true. Multiply 1/4 × 8 = 2.
